newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up led by blue chips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on Thursday as buyers paid premiums for selected blue chips and automation improved trading, brokers said.

The all share index closed 5.3 points up at 733.8 with price gains outnumbering declines by 34 to 20. Central Finance rose six rupees to 316, Ceylon Oxygen two rupees to 63, Hatton National Bank seven to 260 and John Keells Holdings five to 250.
"Buyers have been puhsed to pay premiums for shares after good corporate results for the year to March and the first quarter of 1997," said Prasanna Chandrasekera of brokerage John Keells.
Turnover was 43.2 million rupees, led by 103,700 Grain Elevators, 540,000 Hotel Services, 121,100 Lanka Lubricants, 16,000 John Keells Holdings.
"Trading is improving due to the automation," said Rohan Fernando of brokerage CT Smith. "There is no time lag unlike before between when a client gives an order and it is executed", he said.
The stock exchange began automation trials on Tuesday ahead of launching full-scale screen-based trading later this month.

The government sold 51 percent in Namunukula Plantations for 40 rupees a share, raising 408 million rupees, which was not included in the day's turnover but shown as an extraordinary item. -- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
